questions.stem: A 37-year-old man presents with three weeks of hemoptysis and gross hematuria. Renal biopsy reveals crescentic glomerulonephritis. Anti-GBM disease is suspected. Anti-GBM disease is best classified as which type of disorder?
explanations: Incorrect. Anti-GBM disease does not arise secondary to infection.
Incorrect. It is not associated with an underlying malignancy.
Correct. Anti-GBM disease is a rare primary autoimmune disorder, considered a primary glomerular disease because it does not arise secondary to infection, cancer, or systemic disease.
Incorrect. The brick does not describe drug exposure as the cause.
Incorrect. Although type IV collagen is the antigen, the disorder is autoimmune, not inherited.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with hemoptysis is found to have rapidly rising creatinine and hematuria. Anti-GBM disease is on the differential. Anti-GBM disease belongs to which group of disorders that involve both kidney and lung?
explanations: Correct. Anti-GBM disease is one of the pulmonary-renal syndromes, which cause disease in both the lungs and kidneys.
Incorrect. Cardiorenal syndromes involve heart-kidney interactions, not lung-kidney.
Incorrect. Hepatorenal syndrome involves liver disease leading to kidney failure.
Incorrect. Tubulointerstitial syndromes affect renal tubules, not lung-kidney.
Incorrect. Anti-GBM disease classically presents with nephritic, not nephrotic, syndrome.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old male smoker presents with hemoptysis, hematuria, and acute kidney injury. Anti-GBM antibodies target which specific antigen?
explanations: Correct. Anti-GBM antibodies form against the alpha 3 chain of type IV collagen present in the basement membranes of glomeruli and pulmonary alveoli.
Incorrect. Type III collagen is not the anti-GBM antigen.
Incorrect. PLA2R is the antigen in primary membranous nephropathy.
Incorrect. Anti-dsDNA is the autoantibody of lupus nephritis.
Incorrect. Proteinase 3 is targeted in granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA).

questions.stem: An immunology lecture covers the mechanism by which anti-GBM antibodies damage glomerular and alveolar tissue. Anti-GBM disease is an example of which type of hypersensitivity reaction?
explanations: Incorrect. Type I is IgE-mediated (e.g., anaphylaxis).
Incorrect. Type V (stimulatory) reactions are not implicated in anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. Type III involves circulating immune complexes (e.g., postinfectious GN, lupus); anti-GBM has linear, not granular, deposition.
Incorrect. Type IV is T cell-mediated (e.g., contact dermatitis).
Correct. Anti-GBM disease is a type II hypersensitivity reaction, in which IgG antibodies attack cellular or extracellular matrix antigens, producing cell and tissue damage.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man and a 65-year-old woman are both diagnosed with anti-GBM disease. Which presentation is more typical of the younger patient?
explanations: Incorrect. Isolated glomerulonephritis is more common in older patients (>50 years).
Incorrect. Nephrotic-range proteinuria is not characteristic of anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. Anti-GBM disease typically presents with active nephritic features, not asymptomatic proteinuria.
Correct. Younger patients (<30 years) are more likely to present with pulmonary hemorrhage, while older patients (>50 years) more often have isolated glomerulonephritis.
Incorrect. Tubular acidosis is not a feature of anti-GBM disease.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man develops hematuria, edema, hypertension, and a rapidly rising serum creatinine over two weeks. Anti-GBM disease is suspected. Which renal syndrome best describes this presentation?
explanations: Incorrect. Nephrotic syndrome features heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and edema without prominent hematuria or RPGN.
Correct. Anti-GBM disease classically presents as nephritic syndrome with gross hematuria, edema, and hypertension, often as rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN).
Incorrect. The presentation includes systemic features and rapidly declining GFR, not isolated hematuria.
Incorrect. Tubulointerstitial nephritis presents with sterile pyuria and tubular dysfunction, not RPGN.
Incorrect. Renal artery stenosis causes hypertension but not hematuria or nephritic sediment.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with anti-GBM disease and a creatinine that has tripled over two weeks. The clinician describes the disorder as one of the most aggressive nephritic disorders. What term best characterizes this rapid decline in renal function?
explanations: Incorrect. Chronic glomerulonephritis develops slowly over years.
Incorrect. Membranous nephropathy is a nephrotic disease, not RPGN.
Correct. Anti-GBM disease is one of the most aggressive nephritic disorders and is characterized by rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) with rapidly declining GFR.
Incorrect. Minimal change disease causes nephrotic syndrome without rapid GFR decline.
Incorrect. Diabetic nephropathy is a slowly progressive sclerosing process.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old smoker presents with three weeks of cough, hemoptysis, dyspnea, and chest pain. Imaging shows diffuse alveolar opacities. About what percentage of anti-GBM patients develop this type of lung damage?
explanations: Incorrect. The brick cites a higher percentage than this.
Incorrect. The brick cites a higher percentage than this.
Incorrect. The brick cites a higher percentage than this.
Correct. Alveolar hemorrhage occurs in approximately 60% of patients with anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. The brick cites 60%, not 90%.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man with anti-GBM disease has alveolar hemorrhage and dyspnea. Which factor is thought to make pulmonary basement membranes susceptible to antibody damage in some patients?
explanations: Incorrect. The brick does not mention altitude.
Incorrect. Thyroid disease is not associated with anti-GBM lung involvement.
Incorrect. Exercise is not implicated in alveolar membrane susceptibility.
Incorrect. Diet is not described as a trigger.
Correct. Lung damage from smoking is thought to be needed in some patients to make alveolar basement membranes accessible to circulating anti-GBM autoantibodies.

questions.stem: Several new cases of anti-GBM disease were reported in London during the COVID-19 outbreak in 2019-2020. This cluster supports which proposed contributor to disease onset?
explanations: Incorrect. The brick highlights an environmental trigger, not solely genetics.
Correct. The London cluster during COVID-19 supports the premise that environmental factors such as infection may trigger anti-GBM disease in susceptible individuals.
Incorrect. Vaccine reactions are not cited in the brick.
Incorrect. Occupational toxins are not the trigger described.
Incorrect. Dietary deficiencies are not implicated.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with anti-GBM disease undergoes renal biopsy. Light microscopy shows extensive glomerular crescents. Which renal histologic pattern does this represent?
explanations: Incorrect. Minimal change shows normal light microscopy with foot process effacement on EM.
Incorrect. Membranous nephropathy shows thickened GBM without crescents.
Correct. Anti-GBM disease produces crescentic glomerulonephritis, characterized by extensive glomerular crescents on light microscopy.
Incorrect. FSGS shows segmental sclerosis without crescents.
Incorrect. Mesangial proliferation alone is not the hallmark of anti-GBM disease.

questions.stem: A pathologist describes the cellular composition of glomerular crescents in a patient with anti-GBM disease. Which combination of components are crescents made of?
choices: Mesangial cells with amyloid fibril deposits
explanations: Correct. Crescents form from ruptured glomerular capillaries and consist of glomerular epithelial cells, fibrin, plasma proteins, monocytes, macrophages, and other inflammatory cells.
Incorrect. Crescents are not composed primarily of endothelial cells and platelets.
Incorrect. Mesangial cells and amyloid characterize different glomerular processes.
Incorrect. Foam cells and lipid are not the constituents of crescents.
Incorrect. Eosinophils and IgE are not components of crescents.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man with hemoptysis, hematuria, and ANA/ANCA-negative serologies undergoes renal biopsy. Immunofluorescence reveals which pattern characteristic of anti-GBM disease?
explanations: Incorrect. Granular deposits are seen in immune complex diseases such as postinfectious GN or lupus, not anti-GBM.
Incorrect. Tram-tracking is a light microscopy finding in membranoproliferative GN.
Incorrect. Pauci-immune staining is the hallmark of ANCA-associated vasculitis.
Correct. Anti-GBM disease shows a linear, ribbon-like pattern of IgG deposition along the basement membrane on immunofluorescence, distinguishing it from other glomerulonephritides.
Incorrect. Subepithelial humps describe postinfectious GN on EM.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman with anti-GBM disease has alveolar hemorrhage. RBCs and hemoglobin clog the alveoli. Which pulmonary physiologic abnormality is most likely?
explanations: Incorrect. Diffusing capacity decreases, not increases, although DLCO can paradoxically appear elevated acutely from blood in alveoli (not described here).
Incorrect. The brick attributes findings to alveolar hemorrhage, not pleural effusion.
Incorrect. The brick describes a diffusion abnormality, not airway obstruction.
Incorrect. Pulmonary hypertension is not described as the primary abnormality.
Correct. Alveolar hemorrhage clogs alveoli with RBCs and hemoglobin, reducing CO2 and O2 transfer (decreased diffusing capacity) and causing hypoxemia and dyspnea.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with rapidly progressive GFR decline and hemoptysis undergoes urinalysis. Which sediment finding most strongly suggests glomerular disease such as anti-GBM?
choices: Dysmorphic RBCs with red cell casts
Waxy casts of chronic kidney disease
explanations: Incorrect. Hyaline casts are nonspecific and seen in normal urine.
Correct. Dysmorphic RBCs and red cell casts are signs of glomerular disease and are typical of anti-GBM disease, which often shows macroscopic hematuria.
Incorrect. Waxy casts indicate chronic kidney disease, not active glomerular inflammation.
Incorrect. Eosinophiluria suggests acute interstitial nephritis.
Incorrect. Crystals reflect stone disease or metabolic disorders, not glomerular injury.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man with suspected anti-GBM disease has serum sent for autoantibody testing. Which serologic test is both sensitive and specific for the diagnosis?
explanations: Incorrect. ANA is sensitive for lupus, not anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. Anti-dsDNA is specific for lupus.
Correct. ELISA for anti-GBM autoantibodies is both sensitive and specific and is ordered when this disease is suspected.
Incorrect. c-ANCA suggests granulomatosis with polyangiitis and is negative in anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. p-ANCA suggests microscopic polyangiitis or EGPA and is negative in anti-GBM disease.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with hemoptysis and acute kidney injury has anti-GBM antibodies sent. The clinician also orders ANCA studies. What is the rationale for this additional testing?
choices: To confirm a diagnosis of lupus nephritis
To detect concurrent IgA nephropathy involvement
To screen for hepatitis C cryoglobulinemia
To distinguish from GPA and MPA vasculitides
explanations: Incorrect. Lupus is screened with ANA and anti-dsDNA, not ANCA.
Incorrect. IgA nephropathy is diagnosed by biopsy, not ANCA.
Incorrect. ANCA does not screen for hepatitis C.

Correct. The presentation of granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is similar to anti-GBM disease, so ANCA studies (c-ANCA and p-ANCA) are ordered to distinguish them; ANCA is negative in anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. Complement levels, not ANCA, assess complement consumption.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with anti-GBM disease undergoes chest CT for hemoptysis. Which finding is most consistent with alveolar hemorrhage?
explanations: Incorrect. A solitary nodule suggests malignancy or granuloma, not alveolar hemorrhage.
Correct. CT imaging in anti-GBM disease typically shows ground-glass opacities or consolidations, while chest x-ray may show patchy or diffuse opacities.
Incorrect. Pleural calcifications suggest prior asbestos exposure or chronic pleural disease.
Incorrect. Honeycombing is a feature of advanced fibrosis (e.g., IPF).
Incorrect. Lymphadenopathy is not described as a typical anti-GBM finding.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with hemoptysis and hematuria has positive serum anti-GBM antibodies. Which test is generally required to confirm the diagnosis and assess disease severity?
explanations: Incorrect. Lung biopsy is less helpful, more invasive, and high risk in patients with pulmonary hemorrhage.
Correct. Renal biopsy showing linear IgG deposition along the GBM on immunofluorescence is generally required to confirm the diagnosis and helps gauge severity and prognosis.
Incorrect. Bone marrow is not involved in anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. Anti-GBM disease does not typically present with skin lesions.
Incorrect. Pleural biopsy is not used to diagnose anti-GBM disease.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with cough, hemoptysis, fever, sinusitis, and a purpuric rash. Renal biopsy shows pauci-immune crescentic GN. Serology is c-ANCA positive. Which diagnosis is most likely?
explanations: Incorrect. Anti-GBM disease is ANCA-negative and shows linear IgG, not pauci-immune staining.
Incorrect. Lupus nephritis is associated with ANA and anti-dsDNA.
Correct. GPA presents with upper respiratory tract symptoms (especially sinusitis), purpuric rash, and pulmonary-renal involvement; serology shows c-ANCA and anti-proteinase-3 antibodies.
Incorrect. EGPA presents with asthma, allergic rhinitis, nasal polyposis, and p-ANCA.
Incorrect. IgA nephropathy is not associated with sinusitis, hemoptysis, or c-ANCA.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman presents with asthma, allergic rhinitis, nasal polyposis, and pleural effusions. Serology is p-ANCA positive. Which pulmonary-renal syndrome does this best fit?
explanations: Incorrect. Anti-GBM disease lacks asthma and nasal polyposis, and is ANCA-negative.
Incorrect. GPA is associated with c-ANCA and sinusitis/purpura, not asthma and nasal polyposis.
Correct. EGPA classically presents with asthma, pleural effusions, allergic rhinitis, and nasal polyposis, with p-ANCA serology.
Incorrect. Lupus nephritis features ANA/anti-dsDNA and multisystem involvement (rash, arthritis).
Incorrect. Microscopic polyangiitis has p-ANCA but lacks the asthma and nasal polyposis seen in EGPA.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man is diagnosed with anti-GBM disease. He is started on plasmapheresis. What is the purpose of this therapy?
explanations: Incorrect. Plasmapheresis in anti-GBM disease is not used for clotting factor replacement.
Incorrect. Plasmapheresis does not directly restore tubular function.
Incorrect. Plasmapheresis does not stimulate erythropoiesis.
Incorrect. Plasmapheresis does not deliver chemotherapy.
Correct. Plasma exchange separates blood components and removes the autoantibody-filled plasma, replacing it with albumin; it is typically performed 5-7 times per week for 2-3 weeks.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman with anti-GBM disease is started on plasmapheresis and IV methylprednisolone. Which additional immunosuppressant is standardly paired with glucocorticoids in this disease?
explanations: Incorrect. Rituximab is used in some autoimmune diseases but is not the standard agent paired with steroids in this brick.
Correct. Standard therapy combines IV glucocorticoids (e.g., methylprednisolone) with cyclophosphamide, an alkylating agent.
Incorrect. Methotrexate is not the standard agent for anti-GBM disease.
Incorrect. Azathioprine is not the standard initial immunosuppressant cited in the brick.
Incorrect. Mycophenolate mofetil is not the standard initial agent for anti-GBM disease.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with anti-GBM disease presents with serum creatinine of 8.2 mg/dL and requires early dialysis. According to the brick, what does this portend for his renal prognosis?
choices: Renal function will likely not recover
He will fully recover within 1 week
The lung disease will worsen with dialysis
explanations: Incorrect. Once early dialysis is required, renal recovery is unlikely.
Correct. If early dialysis is required, the prognosis is poor and renal function will likely not recover; however, plasmapheresis and immunosuppressants remain effective for the pulmonary hemorrhage.
Incorrect. Rapid full recovery is not expected once dialysis is needed.
Incorrect. Dialysis does not worsen alveolar hemorrhage.
Incorrect. Plasmapheresis is still indicated for the pulmonary disease even when dialysis is required.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman successfully treated for anti-GBM disease is concerned about recurrence. Her antibody titers are now undetectable. According to the brick, what is the expected long-term course?
explanations: Incorrect. The brick states relapses are uncommon after successful treatment.
Incorrect. Lifelong dialysis is not inevitable, particularly when creatinine is below 5.7 mg/dL at presentation.
Correct. After successful treatment, relapses of anti-GBM disease are uncommon.
Incorrect. Routine yearly plasmapheresis is not described as standard maintenance.
Incorrect. The brick does not recommend long-term high-dose steroids as recurrence prevention.
